interior-demolition.deep_content:
Interior demolition is one of the most common precursors to a serious renovation — and one of the most frequently botched when handled by unlicensed operators cutting corners. A true gut job means stripping a space down to the framing: walls, ceilings, flooring, fixtures, built-in cabinetry, and mechanical rough-ins all come out cleanly and safely. C&S Demolition approaches every interior demo with a pre-project walkthrough to identify load-bearing elements, utility lines, and any asbestos or lead-containing materials that require proper abatement before a single sledgehammer swings. Working without that assessment invites structural surprises mid-project and potential hazmat violations.

Cost drivers for interior demolition include the overall square footage, the number of rooms, ceiling height (two-story homes cost more to scaffold safely), the presence of plaster-and-lath versus drywall, and whether hazardous material testing and abatement is needed. Tightly restricted access — narrow staircases, townhomes, occupied adjacent units — adds time and labor. Projects typically run between $1,500 and $8,000 depending on scope, and most complete in one to three days once the site is prepped.

A licensed, insured contractor like C&S handles not just the physical work but the liability that comes with it. We carry workers' comp and general liability, meaning your property and your contractor's crew are covered if the unexpected happens. We sort debris for recycling and haul everything off-site, leaving a clean, broom-swept shell ready for your framers and electricians to walk right in.
included: Removal of walls, ceilings, and flooring

pool-demolition.deep_content:
Pool removal is not a weekend demo project — it is a permitted, engineered scope of work that requires coordination with your local building department before a single piece of equipment enters the yard. C&S Demolition handles the full permitting process: pulling the demolition permit, draining the pool in compliance with local discharge regulations, and working from a plan that either calls for partial removal (break and fill, leaving the bottom shell as a base) or full removal down to native soil. Both methods require engineered compacted backfill and a grading plan that prevents future settlement, which is why unpermitted pool fills consistently cause slab cracking, foundation shifts, and problems at resale.

For partial removal, the pool walls are broken to a specified depth, holes are punched in the floor for drainage, and the void is filled with imported base material compacted in lifts — not just the broken concrete pushed back in. Full removal takes the entire shell out, inspects the sub-grade, and brings in engineered fill. In both cases, the work closes with a final city inspection and sign-off, giving you a recorded permit that fully documents the removal for future buyers, lenders, and insurers.

C&S positions itself as the permitted professional option precisely because the consequences of doing this work without a license and a permit extend years into the future. Settlement claims, failed home sales, and insurance disputes are a predictable result of unpermitted pool fills. We do the job once, by the book, with documentation.
included: Pool draining in compliance with discharge regulations
Partial or full shell removal per engineered plan
Final city inspection and permit sign-off

shed-demolition.deep_content:
Shed, garage, and outbuilding removal looks simple from the outside — four walls, a roof, maybe a concrete floor — but the variables pile up quickly. An older structure may have asbestos-containing roofing panels or fiber cement siding, electrical drops that need to be properly disconnected and capped, or a slab that the client wants removed along with the structure. C&S Demolition arrives with the right equipment for the job: hand tools and a small excavator for tight spaces, larger equipment when the site allows, and a dump truck or roll-off to haul debris rather than staging it on your driveway for three weeks.

The size of the structure, the materials involved (wood frame versus masonry or block), the presence of utilities, and the desired outcome for any existing slab are the primary cost drivers. Simple wood-frame sheds on smaller lots typically sit at the lower end of the $500–$2,500 range, while block or masonry outbuildings with attached concrete work push toward the higher end. Most single-structure removals are completed the same day, with the site graded and raked clean before the crew leaves.

Hiring a licensed contractor matters here even on seemingly minor jobs. An unlicensed operator who disconnects a live electrical service incorrectly or disturbs asbestos-containing roofing without proper containment creates liability that falls on the property owner — not the person they paid. C&S is licensed (CA Lic. #1126325), fully insured, and capable of handling every phase of the project from utility coordination to final debris disposal.
included: Structure teardown (wood, metal, or masonry frame)

deck-demolition.deep_content:
Deck and patio demolition spans a wide range of complexity depending on what was built and how. A simple pressure-treated wood deck bolted to a ledger board is a straightforward teardown. A multi-level composite deck with built-in planters, a pergola overhead, and a poured concrete patio beneath it is a multi-phase project requiring sequenced disassembly, concrete breaking, and careful attention to the existing ledger attachment point on the structure — improper removal can damage exterior sheathing or allow water intrusion into the wall cavity.

Concrete patios add a dimension most homeowners underestimate: slab thickness, reinforcement, and sub-base conditions determine how quickly concrete breaks and how much material needs to be hauled. Reinforced slabs over four inches thick take longer per square foot and produce heavier debris loads. Pergolas and shade structures come down quickly but add volume to the load. Cost factors include total square footage, material mix (wood, composite, concrete, or a combination), access for equipment, and any tie-ins to the main structure that require patching.

C&S Demolition leaves your yard clear and ready for whatever comes next — whether that is a new deck, a landscape install, or a clean slate. We haul all debris off-site the same day, and our crew handles the sequencing that protects your home's exterior envelope from collateral damage during the teardown. The project range runs $800–$3,500 and most jobs complete in one to two days.
included: Wood, composite, or aluminum deck teardown
Ledger board removal and exterior patching

wall-removal.deep_content:
Load-bearing wall removal is structural work — and treating it as anything less is how renovations end up with cracked drywall, sagging ceilings, and emergency engineering calls six months after the fact. Before any wall comes down, C&S Demolition conducts a thorough structural assessment to determine load paths, identify the beam sizing required for the new opening, and confirm that the foundation below can accept the point loads that will result from the new header configuration. This work is coordinated with a licensed structural engineer when required, and permit applications are submitted to the local building department before demolition begins.

The removal itself involves shoring the ceiling above the opening while the existing framing comes out, installing the engineered header or flush beam on properly sized posts, and verifying that the new assembly passes rough framing inspection. Mechanical, electrical, and plumbing runs through the existing wall are identified beforehand and either relocated or capped per code. Drywall, insulation, and finish work are not part of a demolition scope, but the opening left behind is clean, plumb, and ready for your finish contractor.

Project costs range from $1,200 to $5,000 depending on wall length, beam span, the number of mechanical systems that need to be relocated, and whether an engineering stamp is required. This is not a scope to hand to a handyman or an unlicensed subcontractor. The structural consequences of an under-engineered header or improperly transferred load accumulate over years and become expensive — and dangerous — to correct.
included: Structural assessment and load path analysis
Mechanical, electrical, and plumbing identification and cap-off
Debris removal and rough opening cleanup

concrete-removal.deep_content:
Concrete removal is heavier work than it looks. A standard four-inch residential driveway slab can weigh 50 pounds per square foot — which means a modest 400-square-foot driveway produces roughly ten tons of material that needs to be broken, loaded, and legally disposed of. C&S Demolition uses electric jackhammers, hydraulic breakers, and skid-steer equipment scaled to the job, minimizing vibration damage to adjacent structures and completing the work efficiently rather than spending days grinding through reinforced concrete with undersized tools.

The variables that drive project cost include slab thickness (four inches versus six inches versus an eight-inch commercial pad makes a substantial difference), steel reinforcement (rebar-heavy slabs take longer to break and sort for recycling), site access for equipment, proximity to structures or utilities that require hand-breaking near boundaries, and total volume of material to be hauled. Driveways, patios, sidewalks, and foundations each have their own profile. Aggregate and crushed concrete can often be recycled rather than landfilled, which reduces disposal costs and diverts material from the waste stream.

Unlicensed operators frequently underestimate concrete breaking jobs, show up with undersized equipment, and leave a half-finished pile on your driveway while they sort out logistics. C&S arrives with the right equipment, completes the work on schedule, and leaves the sub-base graded and ready for the next contractor. Projects run $1,000–$6,000 depending on volume and conditions, with most residential scopes finishing in one to two days.
included: Jackhammer and hydraulic breaking of slabs or foundations
Full debris hauling and legal disposal

kitchen-demolition.deep_content:
A kitchen gut is more than pulling out cabinets — it involves careful sequencing to protect plumbing lines, gas connections, and electrical circuits while clearing the space completely for a new layout. C&S Demolition coordinates utility shutoffs before any work begins, removes appliances safely (including disconnecting gas ranges and securing refrigerant lines on built-in refrigerators), and takes down every cabinet, countertop, backsplash tile, and flooring layer the project scope calls for. We identify the substrate condition underneath tile and flooring so your general contractor walks in with accurate information rather than surprises.

Kitchen demolition costs are driven by kitchen size, ceiling height, the number of cabinets and linear feet of countertop, flooring type and layers (multiple layers of flooring over older sub-floor add significant labor), and whether the tile backsplash extends to full-height or covers only a partial wall. Hazardous material considerations are real in older kitchens: vinyl tile from pre-1980 construction commonly contains asbestos, and lead paint is possible in homes built before 1978. C&S handles testing coordination and can oversee or perform abatement when flagged.

Projects run $1,500–$5,000 and typically complete in one to two days. The value of using a licensed, insured crew for kitchen demo comes into sharp focus when a plumber, electrician, or general contractor walks in afterward and finds the site in documented, clean condition — no active gas leaks, no disturbed asbestos, no hidden damage. We turn over a broom-clean shell with every mechanical penetration properly capped and labeled.
included: Gas, water, and electrical shutoff coordination

bathroom-demolition.deep_content:
Bathroom demolition involves tearing out some of the most labor-intensive finish work in a home — ceramic and porcelain tile set in mortar beds, cast-iron or steel tubs bonded to surrounding tile, toilet flanges and wax rings, vanity tops, and the wet-area backer board behind it all. C&S Demolition approaches bathroom demo with a sharp eye on the substrate: discovering that a shower pan has leaked into the sub-floor, or that the original mortar bed extends three inches thick rather than the typical half-inch of modern tile board, changes the scope and the timeline. We communicate those findings in real time so your tile contractor and general contractor are never caught off guard.

Key cost factors include bathroom size, whether the scope includes full tile removal to bare studs (versus surface-only), the presence of a cast-iron tub versus a fiberglass unit (cast iron requires cutting and special handling), plumbing stub-out coordination, and any evidence of mold or water damage in the walls requiring additional remediation steps. Older bathrooms frequently have asbestos-containing floor tile or textured ceilings that require certified abatement before demo proceeds.

Most bathroom demos complete in a single day for a standard full bath, with more complex spa-style bathrooms or full-tile rooms running into a second day. Projects range from $800–$3,500. C&S carries the insurance and holds the license that protects both the homeowner and the downstream trade contractors who rely on a clean, accurately documented teardown as their starting point.
included: Full tile removal to studs or sub-floor
Sub-floor assessment and removal if damaged

garage-demolition.deep_content:
Detached garage demolition is a mid-scale project that combines structural teardown, concrete slab work, and utility disconnection in one scope. Before any framing comes down, the electrical service to the structure must be properly disconnected at the panel and any sub-panel removed — a step that requires coordination with the utility and should never be improvised by an unlicensed crew. Gas lines serving a garage heater or workshop equipment are similarly capped under permit. Once utilities are cleared, framing, roofing, and siding come down in sequence, and the concrete slab is either broken and hauled or left in place per the project plan.

Cost drivers include the size of the structure (single-car versus two-car or larger), roofing material (composite shingles versus tile or metal), the presence of a masonry or stucco exterior versus wood frame, whether the slab is being removed, and any asbestos-containing materials in roofing, insulation, or drywall that require abatement. Access for a skid steer or small excavator reduces labor time significantly on larger structures; tight sites with limited gate access require more hand labor and longer timelines.

C&S Demolition handles the full sequence from permit to final cleanup for garage demolition projects ranging from $2,500–$8,000. Most complete in one to two days. The licensed, insured approach matters particularly here because improperly disconnected electrical services, disturbed asbestos, and unpermitted concrete removal can all create title and insurance issues on your property that outlast the project by years.
included: Electrical and gas disconnection under permit
Full framing, roofing, and siding teardown

selective-demolition.deep_content:
Selective demolition is the art of removing exactly what needs to go while protecting everything around it. This is common in commercial tenant improvement projects, historic remodels, multi-family renovations, and any situation where a building is occupied or partially operational during construction. The challenge is precision: opening one wall for MEP rough-in without damaging adjacent finishes, removing a portion of a concrete slab while maintaining the structural integrity of the surrounding floor, or extracting outdated mechanical equipment from a tight mechanical room without damaging the building envelope.

The breadth of selective demo work means that cost and duration vary enormously — from $1,000 for a focused single-wall opening to $10,000 or more for a complex multi-zone commercial renovation. Accurate scoping requires a pre-project site walk with the GC and design team to document exactly what is being preserved, what is being removed, and how the transition zone will be protected. Dust containment, vibration control, and noise ordinance compliance are all considerations that a professional selective demo contractor builds into the work plan rather than discovering them mid-project.

C&S Demolition brings the licensed commercial contractor experience that selective work demands. We work alongside GCs, MEP subcontractors, and owners' representatives with clear scope documentation, proper insurance certificates, and the field judgment to stop and communicate when actual conditions differ from what was shown on drawings. Unlicensed operators on selective demo jobs frequently cause damage that exceeds the original demo contract value — the precision required here makes licensing and experience non-negotiable.
included: Pre-project scope walkthrough with GC and design team
Dust and debris containment in occupied areas
Precision removal of targeted walls, floors, or ceilings
Debris hauling with minimal disruption to operations

flooring-removal.deep_content:
Flooring removal is often the first and fastest phase of a renovation, but the range of what falls under that heading — ceramic tile in mortar beds, glued-down hardwood, stapled carpet over multiple layers of older vinyl, or engineered flooring on floating underlayment — means that the labor involved varies by an order of magnitude from one floor to the next. C&S Demolition assesses the floor assembly before quoting: a single layer of floating laminate over a concrete slab comes up in hours, while a 1970s-era kitchen floor with three generations of vinyl and a thick mortar bed can take a full day just for one room.

Asbestos-containing resilient flooring is a real concern in California homes built before 1980. Vinyl composition tile, sheet vinyl, and the mastic adhesives used to bond them frequently contain asbestos fibers that are regulated under California law. C&S coordinates certified asbestos testing when there is any indication of pre-1980 materials, and we do not disturb suspect materials until clearance is confirmed. This step protects your household, your future contractors, and your legal standing as a property owner.

Project costs run from $500–$3,000 depending on flooring type, square footage, number of layers, and whether sub-floor repair or leveling is needed after removal. Most single-area jobs complete the same day. We haul all material off-site, leave the sub-floor swept and documented, and give your installer the clean, prepared surface they need to start immediately.
included: Removal of tile, hardwood, carpet, vinyl, or laminate
Asbestos testing coordination for pre-1980 materials

driveway-removal.deep_content:
Driveway removal is a volume game: breaking the slab is often faster than loading and hauling it. A standard two-car asphalt driveway can produce five to eight tons of material, while a comparable concrete driveway with rebar reinforcement may produce twelve tons or more at a higher density. C&S Demolition scales equipment to the job — a skid-steer with a hydraulic breaker attachment on a wide driveway, hand equipment near garage aprons, landscaping, or utilities where precision matters. The goal is always to leave the sub-grade clean and at the right elevation for the new pour or pave, not just to clear the surface.

Key cost factors include total square footage, thickness (four-inch residential versus six-inch or eight-inch commercial-grade slabs), reinforcement level (wire mesh versus rebar grid), sub-base conditions, proximity of landscaping or underground utilities that require careful hand-work, and whether site access allows a truck to pull close for direct loading. Asphalt and concrete recycling options are available and can offset disposal costs on larger projects.

Properly permitted driveway removal is often required when the work connects to a public sidewalk or curb, as the city wants documentation that the public right-of-way is protected during work and restored afterward. C&S handles that coordination with your local public works department. Projects range from $800–$4,000 and most complete in one to two days, leaving the surface graded and ready for your paving or concrete contractor.
included: Hydraulic breaking of asphalt or concrete surface
Rebar separation and recycling where applicable
Site cleanup and final grade verification

chimney-demolition.deep_content:
Chimney demolition is one of the more technically demanding residential demo tasks because it involves structural masonry that passes through multiple floor levels, ties into the roof framing, and often has a firebox and hearth assembly at the base that is built into the foundation or first-floor slab. A chimney is not simply knocked over — it is disassembled from the top down, brick by brick or with controlled mechanical equipment where access permits, with careful attention to where the masonry ties into the roof structure and the ceiling framing below. Improper chimney removal is a common source of roof leaks, structural gaps in the framing, and incomplete fire-stopping that creates code violations in the wall cavity.

The scope commonly includes the exterior chimney stack above the roofline, the chase passing through interior floors and attic space, the firebox, damper assembly, and hearth at the base level, and the concrete or masonry foundation extension below. Each zone has different materials and different access constraints. Older brick chimneys may contain asbestos-containing refractory mortar or insulation within the flue, requiring testing before debris is disturbed.

Cost ranges from $1,500–$6,000 depending on chimney height, the number of floors it passes through, firebox and hearth scope, access for equipment or manual labor on the roof, and whether any structural patching at the roof plane or floor framing is required after removal. Most jobs complete in one to two days. C&S provides a finished scope that leaves roof penetration patched, framing intact, and the wall cavity properly fire-stopped.
included: Top-down masonry disassembly of chimney stack
Flue liner and chase teardown through interior floors
Asbestos testing coordination for refractory materials
Full debris hauling and site cleanup

commercial-demolition.deep_content:
Commercial demolition requires a different level of coordination, documentation, and contractor qualification than residential work. A retail build-out gut, office space conversion, or industrial interior demolition involves multiple trade subcontractors, often an occupied adjacent tenant, and a building department that wants to see a licensed general or specialty contractor on the permit — not a day-labor crew with a rented dumpster. C&S Demolition holds a California contractor's license and carries the general liability and workers' compensation coverage that commercial landlords, property managers, and GCs require before issuing a subcontract or allowing access to a commercial property.

The scope of commercial demolition varies from a targeted retail storefront gut (removing all interior finishes down to the structural shell) to full floor-plate demolition in multi-tenant office buildings, healthcare facility tenant improvements, or warehouse-to-flex conversions. Each project starts with a pre-construction coordination meeting, an existing-conditions review, and a scope document that defines exactly what is being demoed, what is being protected, and what the handoff condition to the next trade will be. Asbestos-containing materials, lead paint, and other regulated substances must be abated under permit before demolition begins — C&S manages or coordinates that abatement phase to keep the project on schedule.

Cost drivers include gross square footage, number of interior partition systems, the presence of suspended ceilings and raised floors, MEP density, regulated material abatement scope, project schedule constraints, and site access logistics in occupied or multi-story buildings. Projects range from $3,000 for a small tenant improvement to $25,000 or more for large-floor-plate or multi-phase commercial scopes. C&S delivers a documented, clean shell that passes inspection and gives the next phase a professional starting point.
included: Permit application and licensed contractor documentation
Full interior partition, ceiling, and flooring removal
MEP stub-out identification, capping, and labeling
Debris hauling, recycling, and documented disposal

mobile-home-demolition.deep_content:
Mobile home and manufactured home demolition is a specialized scope that differs significantly from site-built residential demo. Manufactured homes use lightweight steel chassis, engineered wood components, and proprietary utility connections that require a specific disassembly sequence to avoid structural collapse during removal. The electrical, water, and sewer utility connections are disconnected and properly abandoned under permit before the structure is touched, and any propane tanks are cleared by the utility provider. Local jurisdictions typically require a demolition permit, and some require notification to the state HCD (Department of Housing and Community Development) when a licensed manufactured home is being removed from a registered space.

Older manufactured homes — particularly those built before 1980 — frequently contain asbestos in roof coating materials, floor tile, insulation, and textured ceiling panels. C&S coordinates certified asbestos inspection and abatement before demo proceeds, protecting the crew, neighbors, and property owner from regulatory liability. Homes with aluminum wiring, polybutylene plumbing, or formaldehyde-containing composite panels all require careful handling during teardown.

The project scope typically includes utility disconnection, structure teardown, chassis and frame removal, foundation pier or slab clearing, and final site grading. Projects range from $3,000–$12,000 depending on home size, utility disconnect complexity, the amount of regulated material found, and the final site condition required (graded and ready for a new unit, or fully cleared for alternative land use). Most complete in two to three days. C&S provides the documentation chain — permits, abatement clearance, final inspection — that property owners need for clean title and future use of the site.
included: Utility disconnection (electric, gas, water, sewer) under permit
Asbestos and regulated material testing and abatement

fence-removal.deep_content:
Fence and wall removal spans a wide spectrum — from pulling out a rotted wood privacy fence with post-puller equipment to demolishing a six-foot masonry block wall with a skid steer or hydraulic breaker. The distinction matters because the equipment, labor, and disposal costs are different by a factor of three or four. C&S Demolition handles the full range: wood privacy fences, vinyl panel systems, chain-link with concrete footings, wrought iron, and masonry or concrete block walls including low-profile retaining walls that have outlived their usefulness or failed structurally.

Retaining wall removal in particular carries structural implications that homeowners frequently underestimate. A failing retaining wall has often been holding back soil load for years, and removing it without understanding the slope geometry and soil conditions can cause a rapid slope failure. C&S evaluates the site before wall demo begins, confirms that the removal sequence won't destabilize adjacent grades, and advises on temporary slope management when needed. This is not a scope for an unlicensed operator with a pickup truck.

Post footing removal is the most labor-intensive part of most fence removals: concrete footings for wooden or iron fence posts can run 24–36 inches deep, and each one needs to be excavated and removed to allow the new fence contractor to set new posts cleanly. Projects range from $400–$2,500 depending on fence length, material type, footing depth, and whether a masonry wall is involved. Most complete the same day. C&S hauls all debris and leaves the line clean and ready for your new fence installation.
included: Removal of wood, vinyl, chain-link, or iron fence
Masonry and concrete block wall demolition
Concrete post footing excavation and removal
Retaining wall stability assessment prior to demo

addition-demolition.deep_content:
Room addition and sunroom demolition is one of the more legally complex demo scopes in residential construction because many additions — particularly those built in the 1970s through 1990s — were added without permits, without proper tie-ins to the original structure, or with materials and methods that no longer meet code. Removing an unpermitted addition is often required by a new owner's lender or insurer, or as a condition of a re-permit project where the homeowner wants to legalize or upgrade the space. C&S Demolition helps clients navigate the permitting pathway before demolition begins, ensuring the teardown itself is documented and that the resulting condition of the original structure is clearly defined.

The structural connection between the addition and the original house is the critical zone. An addition shares a wall, a roof plane, or a floor system with the main structure — and tearing it away without understanding those connections can leave openings in the building envelope, damage existing framing, or remove load contributions that the main structure was relying on. C&S conducts a pre-demo structural review and coordinates with a licensed engineer when the connection complexity warrants it.

Cost factors include addition size, construction type (light wood frame versus masonry or heavy structural), roofing material, the complexity of the structural connection, any regulated materials discovered, and the required condition of the main structure after removal (patched and weatherproofed versus rough open framing). Projects run $1,500–$8,000 and most complete in one to two days. The licensed, documented approach C&S brings protects the property owner's title and provides a clean record for the building department.
included: Permitting coordination and building department liaison
Structural connection assessment prior to teardown
Full addition framing and roofing removal
Exterior wall patching and weatherproofing at tie-in
Regulated material screening and abatement if needed

stucco-removal.deep_content:
Stucco and drywall removal is common in renovation, mold remediation, and seismic retrofit projects across Southern California, where the combination of aging plaster-and-lath walls, multi-coat stucco exteriors, and years of deferred maintenance creates significant work for demo contractors. Interior drywall removal for a remodel is straightforward — but in older homes, that drywall may have been layered over original plaster and lath, requiring significantly more labor to expose the framing. Exterior stucco removal is a different challenge entirely: multiple coats of stucco over wire lath and building paper, with the outermost coat frequently containing silica dust and potentially asbestos-containing textured finishes in pre-1980 construction.

Mold remediation projects add an important layer of complexity. When stucco or drywall is being removed due to moisture intrusion, the scope must be carefully defined so that affected material is fully removed to unaffected substrate without spreading mold-contaminated dust to clean areas of the building. C&S uses containment barriers, negative air pressure, and proper PPE protocols on mold-related demo to meet California regulatory requirements and protect indoor air quality during and after the project.

Cost drivers include square footage, number of material layers, whether the removal is interior or exterior (exterior stucco removal is significantly more labor-intensive), the presence of hazardous materials requiring certified abatement, and mold containment requirements if applicable. Projects run $600–$3,500 and most complete the same day for interior scopes, with exterior stucco taking longer depending on area. C&S delivers a clean, exposed framing assembly ready for inspection, new insulation, and re-sheathing.
included: Asbestos testing for pre-1980 textured surfaces
Mold containment and negative air pressure protocols
Clean framing exposure ready for inspection

whole-house-demolition.deep_content:
Whole house demolition is the most regulated, most coordinated, and most consequential scope in residential demolition. Before a machine touches the structure, a mandatory California pre-demolition asbestos and hazardous materials survey must be completed by a certified inspector, any regulated materials must be abated and cleared, and a demolition permit must be issued by the local building department. Utility disconnects — gas, electric, water, and sewer — must be confirmed in writing by each respective utility provider. C&S Demolition manages every step of this pre-construction sequence, turning what would otherwise be a multi-week coordination headache for a homeowner into a single-point-of-contact managed project.

The demolition itself is typically executed with an excavator equipped with a mechanical claw for controlled structure takedown, followed by a sorting operation that separates recyclable wood, metal, and masonry from general demolition debris. California's recycling requirements for demolition waste mandate that a specified percentage of materials be diverted from landfill, and C&S tracks and documents material diversion in compliance with local ordinance. The site is then graded, compacted, and cleared to the condition specified in the permit — whether that is bare sub-grade ready for new footings or a fully graded lot ready for a new foundation layout.

Cost factors include the size of the structure, story count, construction type (wood frame versus concrete block or masonry), regulated material abatement scope, utility disconnect complexity, hauling distance, and required final site condition. Projects range from $8,000 for a small single-story to $35,000 or more for a large or complex home, and most complete in two to five days for the physical demolition once pre-construction requirements are cleared. C&S provides the complete documentation package — permits, abatement clearances, utility disconnects, and final inspection sign-off — for a clean title record.
included: Pre-demolition asbestos and hazmat survey coordination
Permit application and utility disconnect management
Full mechanical demolition with excavator and sorting
California demolition waste recycling and diversion compliance
Site grading and compaction to permit-specified condition
Complete permit documentation and final inspection sign-off
